title: Animated infographic loop
summary: Bring an existing still infographic, diagram or poster to life as a short seamless loop (GIF or MP4) for a README, docs page or social post: the picture's own components move along its story while every label stays exact and legible.

en: make this image move as a loop

notFor.when: a photo of a person should talk or move like a presenter
a new explainer film with a voice-over teaches how something works, rather than animating one existing still
kinetic type, an ident or a motion piece designed from scratch to music, not driven by an existing picture

qa: Every label in every frame matches the source still letter for letter
The components named in the motion list move in the order the story says; nothing outside the list moves
The last frame equals the first: the loop seam is invisible
The GIF stays under 10 MB at the shipped width

intake.ask: Which parts should move, in what order, and what story does the loop tell?
intake.why: The motion list is the brief: it is checked against the render, and it decides layers

intake.ask: Where will it be shown, and at what width and size limit?
intake.why: A README needs a light GIF; a site can take MP4 or WebP
intake.default: README: GIF, 800-960 px wide, 12-15 fps, under 10 MB

intake.ask: Can the components be regenerated or traced as separate layers, or only the flat still exists?
intake.why: Layers make the motion exact; a flat still needs masks or a regenerated plate
intake.default: Regenerate a clean plate and one transparent sprite per component from the still's prompt

profiles.note: README or docs header; a GIF loops forever, so the last frame equals the first. Length band is a house rule, starting point.
